cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What are golden-dataset retrieval evals, and what are they trust infrastructure for?
cards.answer: Trust infrastructure for a retrieval system: real questions labeled with the items required to answer them, scored deterministically, run nightly with regression alerting, with LLM judges reserved for what determinism cannot settle.

cards.heading: The two deterministic metrics
cards.question: What two deterministic metrics form the primary scoring in golden-dataset retrieval evals?
cards.answer: Precision/recall against the items the composer actually selected, and recall at token-budget checkpoints (whether required items survived to the model within budget).

cards.heading: Why degradation is otherwise invisible
cards.question: Why does retrieval quality degrade invisibly without a golden-dataset harness?
cards.answer: No user files a ticket saying the context was slightly worse this week, and standard APM sees traffic but not prompts — nothing else surfaces the degradation.

cards.heading: Role of LLM judges
cards.question: When do LLM judges enter a golden-dataset retrieval eval, given the deterministic metrics already used?
cards.answer: Only where rules cannot decide the question — determinism handles everything it can, because it keeps the signal cheap, stable, and diffable.

cards.heading: When to build the harness
cards.question: What is the ordering advice for when to build a golden-dataset retrieval harness?
cards.answer: Build it before the third retrieval strategy, not after the thirtieth — you cannot safely refactor what you do not measure, and by the thirtieth strategy the system is too entangled to attribute regressions.
